passage:
Salma: Liz, that thing in the lab today. You didn't have to say all that to Rohan.
Elizabeth: He was blaming you for the group report and you did half of it. Somebody had to say it.
Salma: My hands were shaking. I couldn't get one word out.
Elizabeth: I saw. It's okay 🙂
Salma: Thank you. Really. 🤍 I'll borrow your notes and NOT lose them, promise.
Elizabeth: you lost them once lol
Salma: ONCE. Fine. Let me buy you chai on Friday, and when you present next week I'm sitting in the front row.
Elizabeth: Deal 😊
Salma: And if anyone ever talks over you, I'm the loud one this time.

qa.q: What had Rohan blamed Salma for?
qa.a: The group report. Elizabeth says Salma did half of it.

qa.q: What was Salma feeling in the lab, according to the chat?
qa.a: Frozen and anxious. Salma's hands were shaking and Salma couldn't get one word out.

qa.q: How does Salma show that Elizabeth's help is not taken for granted?
qa.a: Salma says thank you, offers chai on Friday, promises to sit in the front row for Elizabeth's presentation, and promises to speak up for Elizabeth next time.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Elizabeth to speak up in front of the lab?
qa.a: Probably nerve-racking, though Elizabeth plays it down in the chat. Elizabeth likely wanted Salma to feel backed up rather than alone with the blame. 🤍

grounding: A friend stands up for Salma in a hard moment and Salma answers with gratitude and a way to return it.

passage:
"Jyoti, wait up!" Imran caught her at the canteen steps. "About what happened in the seminar."
"The Kulkarni thing? Forget it."
"I can't. Everyone laughed when he said my presentation sounded like a village radio announcer. And you just stood up and said, 'Can we discuss the content instead of his accent?'"
"It was a rude comment. Somebody had to say it."
"Nobody else did." Imran rubbed his neck. "I froze. I've been thinking about it all night. Thank you."
"You'd do the same."
"I'd like to think so. So, you're doing the stats project alone, right? I'm good with the regression part. Let me help this weekend."
Jyoti laughed. "Are you paying me back?"
"No. I just want to be the kind of friend you were today. And chai's on me, every Friday till exams."
"Now that's a deal."

qa.q: What did Kulkarni say about Imran's presentation?
qa.a: That it sounded like a village radio announcer.

qa.q: How did Imran feel after Jyoti spoke up?
qa.a: Grateful, and still a little shaken; he had frozen in the seminar and thought about it all night.

qa.q: How does Imran return Jyoti's support?
qa.a: In his own way: offering to help with the regression part of her stats project and buying chai every Friday till exams.

qa.q: How does Jyoti see what she did?
qa.a: As simply necessary ("Somebody had to say it"), not a favour that needs repaying.

grounding: Shows a friend standing up for you in a hard moment, and responding with gratitude and returning it in your own way.

passage:
When our team lead blamed me in front of everyone for the lost client file last month, Farida said, "Actually, it was on the shared drive; the access changed on Monday." She didn't have to. She'd joined only three weeks earlier, and the lead is not someone you contradict.
The worst part is how I reacted. A quick "thanks, yaar" at the lift, and then I got busy. When she asked me a week later to review her slides, I said I didn't have time. Somewhere in my head I'd decided that's just what friends do, so it didn't count.
Then I heard she'd been left off the offsite list. Probably not because of me, but it made me stop.
I booked a coffee with her, told her plainly that her standing up for me mattered, and spent Saturday going through her slides line by line. She sent a photo of her printed deck with a tiny heart drawn in the corner.
— Seema

qa.q: What did Farida tell the team lead about the file?
qa.a: That it was on the shared drive and the access changed on Monday.

qa.q: Why did Seema brush off Farida's help at first?
qa.a: Seema half-assumed that friends just do that, so it didn't count; looking back, Seema feels ashamed of that careless reaction.

qa.q: How did Seema finally return the support?
qa.a: By telling Farida plainly over coffee that it mattered, and spending Saturday reviewing her slides line by line.

qa.q: How might Farida have felt when Seema said there was no time for her slides?
qa.a: Hurt and taken for granted, since she had risked contradicting the lead for Seema.

grounding: Illustrates being defended by a friend, first treating it as owed, then feeling grateful and returning it.
